8. Tables & Reporting

Replacements for PROC REPORT and PROC TABULATE.

The Grammar of Tables (gt)

The gt package allows you to construct tables by adding layers, similar to how ggplot2 builds plots.

library(gt)
library(dplyr)

# Prepare data
summary_table <- adae %>%
  group_by(AESOC) %>%
  summarise(
    n_events = n(),
    n_subjects = n_distinct(USUBJID)
  )

# Create Table
summary_table %>%
  gt() %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "Adverse Events by SOC"
  ) %>%
  cols_label(
    AESOC = "System Organ Class",
    n_events = "Total Events",
    n_subjects = "Total Subjects"
  )

Clinical Reporting: tfrmt and gtsummary

For standard “Table 1” (Demographics), gtsummary is magic.

library(gtsummary)

dm %>%
  select(AGE, SEX, ARM) %>%
  tbl_summary(by = ARM) %>%
  add_p()

Visualization: ggplot2

Replacing PROC SGPLOT.

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(data = dm, aes(x = ARM, y = AGE)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Age Distribution by Arm")

Exporting Reports

Quarto (what you are reading now) is the replacement for ODS. You combine code, text, and output into one HTML, PDF, or Word document.
